evals.prompt: I have an Intel Core Ultra laptop running Ubuntu 24.04. Install OpenClaw for me and run it against a small local model, Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, no prompts please.
evals.expected_output: A single install.sh command using --harness openclaw, --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct and --non-interactive, followed by an ./install.sh status check.
expectations: Uses ./install.sh with --harness openclaw and --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
Adds --non-interactive (or sets HARNESS_AGENT and HARNESS_HF_MODEL with --non-interactive)
Does not install Docker or Node.js by hand, because install.sh runs startup.sh itself
Suggests ./install.sh status to verify the result
Mentions that the endpoint binds to 127.0.0.1 by default

evals.prompt: We already run vLLM at http://10.0.0.5:8000/v1 behind an API key. I want Hermes on this box to use it through the Intel router without starting any local model server. The model it serves is meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct.
evals.expected_output: Set HARNESS_LLM_ROUTER_ENDPOINT, HARNESS_LLM_ROUTER_API_KEY and HARNESS_LLM_MODEL to the exact served id, then run install.sh with --harness hermes and without --model. States that OVMS is not started.
expectations: Sets HARNESS_LLM_ROUTER_ENDPOINT to http://10.0.0.5:8000/v1
Sets HARNESS_LLM_ROUTER_API_KEY rather than writing the key into a file or command history
Passes --harness hermes and sets HARNESS_LLM_MODEL=meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct without --model, because --model would strip the org/ prefix
States that OVMS is not started and the installer does not health-check the external endpoint
Notes that Hermes onboarding only prints the endpoint and the user must configure the provider in ~/.hermes/config.yaml

evals.prompt: Install deepagents-code and pull the model with the ollama hub: qwen2.5:7b. Will the agent be able to use it?
evals.expected_output: Uses --model-hub ollama with --model qwen2.5:7b, and explains that the model is downloaded and tracked but not served by OVMS, so the agent cannot use it. Recommends the default openvino hub with a Hugging Face id instead.
expectations: Uses --model-hub ollama and --model qwen2.5:7b
States clearly that Ollama models are not served by OVMS and agents will not use them
Suggests the default openvino hub with an org/name Hugging Face id as the working alternative
Mentions ./install.sh models list shows the model as not served by OVMS

evals.prompt: ./install.sh dies on our Linux server with 'syntax error near unexpected token'. I cloned the repo on Windows and copied it over with scp.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses CRLF line endings and gives a fix that converts the scripts to LF or re-clones with the right autocrlf setting.
expectations: Identifies CRLF line endings from the Windows checkout as the likely cause
Gives a concrete fix such as sed -i 's/\r$//' on the scripts or re-cloning with core.autocrlf=input
Does not suggest editing the installer logic or reinstalling Docker

evals.prompt: dcode installed fine but when I run it I get MissingCredentialsError, and on the corp network it also says the server did not become healthy, last status 403.
evals.expected_output: Explains both dcode issues: export HARNESS_DCODE_API_KEY with any non-empty value, and run dcode with the proxy variables unset.
expectations: Tells the user to export HARNESS_DCODE_API_KEY=not-needed (any non-empty value)
Explains that only the installer's smoke test sets that variable
Gives the env -u http_proxy -u https_proxy -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY dcode command for the 403
Explains the 403 comes from the local health check being sent through the proxy

evals.prompt: Remove everything agent-harness-install put on this machine for OpenClaw, but keep the downloaded models.
evals.expected_output: Runs ./uninstall.sh --yes --harness openclaw --keep-models, and lists what stays behind.
expectations: Uses ./uninstall.sh with --yes and --harness openclaw
Passes --keep-models so the downloaded models are retained
Lists what is left in place, including Docker, Node.js/nvm, pulled images and ~/.openclaw
Does not tell the user to delete ~/.agent-harness-install by hand

evals.prompt: Install the Intel GPU kernel driver and the Level-Zero and OpenCL compute runtime on my Ubuntu box so the Arc card shows up under /dev/dri.
evals.expected_output: The skill must not trigger: it only detects GPU readiness and never installs drivers.
expectations: Does not run or recommend ./install.sh as the way to install GPU drivers
Does not claim agent-harness-install installs the Intel GPU driver or compute runtime

evals.prompt: How do I write a custom tool for an OpenClaw agent that calls my REST API?
evals.expected_output: The skill must not trigger: this is a question about the agent itself, not about installing it.
expectations: Does not run or recommend ./install.sh
Does not present installer flags as the answer
